# Three Dividend-paying Technology Leaders to Buy Amid AI


By:[Paul Dykewicz](https://www.dividendinvestor.com/author/pdykewicz-admin/)


, October 23, 2026


Link copied!


Three[dividend-paying](https://www.dividendinvestor.com/three-dividend-paying-data-center-investments-can-rebound/) technology leaders to buy amid AI give investors a chance to catch the next upswing in their share prices.


Following a sharp correction in semiconductor and hardware technology stocks, including a roughly 10% recent pullback in the equities of the semiconductor-capital equipment category, investors have increasingly focused on potential downside scenarios, according to an Oct. 22 Citi Research note. Although the current cycle is fueled by strong artificial intelligence (AI) demand, Citi Research wrote that it sees parallels to the 2020-22 Covid period, when supply shocks and shortages of integrated circuits (ICs) and subsystems constrained WFE growth despite robust underlying demand.


Key risks that could impede the technology leaders from achieving potential target price objectives include competition from rivals, foundry inventory correction risk on 10nm/7nm and the rate of adoption for new Gen 4/5 and extreme ultraviolet (EUV) products, Citi Research wrote. However, a benefit for income investors is that each of the three technology leaders pays dividends.


**Three Dividend-paying Technology Leaders to Buy: KLAC**


KLA Corp. (NASDAQ: KLAC) is “particularly attractive” because it dominates critical segments of semiconductor process control, including wafer inspection, defect detection, and metrology, said Dr. Robert Castellano, PhD, a senior analyst with[Gilder’s Technology Report](https://www.gilderreport.com/offer/gilders-tech-report-launch/?source=GTRGURU) . Dr. Castellano, who described KLA Corp. as an “essential equipment supplier,” explained that as manufacturers transition toward gate-all-around transistors, increasingly complex memory architectures, advanced packaging and maintaining acceptable production yields become progressively more difficult.


“This increases the importance of KLA’s inspection and measurement technologies, which help semiconductor manufacturers identify defects before they result in expensive wafer losses,” said Dr. Castellano, who also serves as a senior analyst with advisory services led by futurist George Gilder, including[Gilder’s Moonshots](https://www.gilderreport.com/offer/gilders-moonshots-launch/?source=GURUMS01) ,[Gilder’s Private Reserve](https://www.gilderreport.com/offer/private-default/?source=GURUGPR1) and[Gilder’s Tech Income Accelerator](https://www.gilderreport.com/offer/gilder-tech-report-pro-launch/?source=GTRPROGURU) . “Unlike equipment suppliers whose sales depend heavily on individual deposition or etching process steps, KLA benefits from the increasing complexity of semiconductor manufacturing across multiple technology generations. Its substantial installed base, recurring service revenue, and strong competitive position make it an attractive way to participate in long-term semiconductor capital investment, although equipment spending remains cyclical.”


George Gilder heads *[Gilder’s Technology Report](https://www.gilderreport.com/offer/gilders-tech-report-launch/?source=GTRGURU) .*


Citi Research values KLAC at $290 using a 38x price/earnings multiple on 2028 estimated earnings power, according to an Oct. 22 research note. The investment firm views a 38x multiple, or above a three-year average of 25x, on multiple re-ratings in the group due to growing AI wafer fab equipment (WFE) exposure.


WFE consists of specialized machinery and tools used to process silicon wafers, such as lithography, etch and deposition tools. Vendors of wafer fab equipment help to enable technological innovation, offering tools the major semiconductor customers like Nvidia (NASDAQ: NVDA) and TSMC (NYSE: TSM) need to stay at the cutting edge in AI and electronics. AI’s integration into infrastructure is setting up a growth cycle that is projected at 8% annualized growth through 2029.


KLA Corp., headquartered in Milpitas, California, also has a $200 million second U.S. headquarters in Ann Arbor, Michigan, home of the main campus of the University of Michigan. The company has a projected 12-month dividend yield of 0.62%, according to[www.dividendinvestor.com](https://www.dividendinvestor.com/dividend-quote/klac/) .

**Three Dividend-paying Technology Leaders to Buy: NVDA**


NVIDIA (NASDAQ: NVDA), a multinational technology company headquartered in Santa Clara, California, gained attention recently with its announcement of co-sponsoring a pluggable standard with Cisco Systems Inc. (NASDAQ: CSCO), of San Jose, California. The move was described as “positive” in a recent Citi Research note. Cisco develops, manufactures, and sells hardware, software, telecommunications equipment, and other high-technology services and products focused on networking, cybersecurity, and AI.


NVIDIA is a current buy recommendation of *[Gilder’s Technology Report](https://www.gilderreport.com/offer/gilders-tech-report-launch/?source=GTRGURU)* , and its team of senior analysts. The Gilder group also offers a host of trading services,[Gilder’s Moonshots](https://www.gilderreport.com/offer/gilders-moonshots-launch/?source=GURUMS01) ,[Gilder’s Private Reserve,](https://www.gilderreport.com/offer/private-default/?source=GURUGPR1) and[Gilder’s Tech Income Accelerator](https://www.gilderreport.com/offer/gilder-tech-report-pro-launch/?source=GTRPROGURU) , aimed at helping investors quicken their pace to profitability.


Senior Analyst Dr. Robert Castellano, PhD, is among those who talk favorably about NVIDIA’s prospects for capital appreciation. Nvidia dominates AI data center computing with its graphic processing units (GPUs), integrated systems, and networking technologies, benefiting directly from hyperscaler capital expenditures, Castellano opined.


Following the launch of several personal AI agents recently, including Muse, Dots, Instinct, GrokBot, and GeminiSpark, Citi Research raised its 2030 central processing unit (CPU) target addressable market (TAM) to $300 billion. Unlike chatbots, which remain largely idle between user interactions, always-on agents like Muse can operate continuously, drive a significant increase in inference-related compute, memory, and networking consumption across both enterprise and consumer workloads, Citi Research wrote.


The investment firm reiterated its “Buy” rating on NVDA with a $315 target price. A key reason is rising demand for GPUs, Citi Research wrote.


*Chart courtesy of[www.stockcharts.com](http://www.stockcharts.com/) .*


**Three Dividend-paying Technology Leaders to Buy: TSM**


Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (NYSE: TSM) is described as the manufacturing foundation of artificial intelligence (AI) by Dr. Castellano, a senior analyst with *[Gilder’s Technology Report](https://www.gilderreport.com/offer/gilders-tech-report-launch/?source=GTRGURU)* , also involving Gilder and his team of technology experts and patent holders. Dr. Castellano speaks highly of Taiwan-based TSM.


TSMC occupies one of the most strategically important positions in the global semiconductor industry because it manufactures the advanced processors designed by Santa Clara, California-headquartered Nvidia (NASDAQ: NVDA), Cupertino, California-based Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL) and numerous other technology leaders, Dr. Castellano said. As artificial intelligence expands from training into inference, demand for leading-edge manufacturing technologies, including 3nm, 2nm, and advanced packaging, should continue growing, he added.


“TSMC benefits not only from increasing chip volumes, but also from higher average selling prices associated with more complex manufacturing processes,” Dr. Castellano continued. “Its technological leadership, strong customer relationships, and substantial barriers to entry provide competitive advantages that are difficult for Samsung or Intel to overcome. For investors, TSMC offers direct exposure to the expansion of AI computing without depending on the success of any single chip designer, although geopolitical risk involving Taiwan remains an important consideration.”

One reason is that a Bespoke Investment Group study of historical returns of the S&P 500 after a bull market’s four-year anniversary found that the median return in the following 12 months reached 16.8%, he added.


“When you’re hot, you’re hot,” continued Woods, describing the stock market’s performance by using the title of a country tune sung by Jerry Reed that reached No. 1 on the U.S. Country charts and won a Grammy Award for Best Male Country Vocal Performance.


A second reason Woods forecast stocks would climb is because earnings growth remains robust, despite surging bond yields, soaring oil prices, and a Fed that seems intent on hiking rates. Plus, the key artificial intelligence (AI) trade is staying “strong” and consumer spending remains healthy, he added.

**Three Dividend-paying Technology Stocks to Buy: Geopolitical Risk**


Ukraine announced a week ago that SpaceX had restricted its Starlink military receptors. Its President Volodymyr Zelenskyy is complaining that the Starlink satellite internet network has been throttled down is country to prevent stopping high-speed Russian attack drones that travel at more than 100 mph. U.S. President Donald Trump said limits had been reversed by Elon Musk who owns the satellite system.


President Trump denied instructing the technology billionaire to restrict connectivity to Starlink’s military-grade counterpart, Starshield, then said Thursday, Oct. 22, that Musk had “put it back.” However, civilian deaths have occurred in the meantime, with one instance of a young mother and her baby girl killed while in a public park to gain fresh air.


Russia keeps intensifying its invasion in Ukraine that has included firing on buses and other civilian targets with jet-powered attack drones. Ukraine’s capital of Kyiv has been targeted directly with women, children, and other civilians dying in increased numbers. In response, more than a dozen automated turrets have been deployed around the Ukrainian capital as Russia steps up its use of faster drones that are more difficult for conventional air defenses to intercept.


Ukraine’s Air Force indicated it is using artificial intelligence and machine vision to track targets and aim through its[Sky Sentinel system](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=U5muTgzi-04) to defend against the faster Russian, jet-powered drones, creating a tactical battle in which warfare is moving towards machines fighting machines. The war’s escalation occurred despite recent visits to both nation’s capitals by President Trump’s envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, who sought to broker a peace agreement.


With military action taking place there, the Middle East, and elsewhere, these three dividend-paying technology leaders offer a potential path to profitability. If investors are wary about the ups and downs of the stock market, an alternative is to trade options.
